title: Connectivity property of an encoded graph
statement: Let $v$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $G$ be a graph on the vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,v-1\}$, encoded by assigning a Boolean value to each two-element vertex set. The connectivity property of $G$ is the Boolean value that is true exactly when $G$ is connected.
caveat: The supplied snippet does not include the definition of graph connectedness or how Boolean edge values determine adjacency.
